title: Why a Doorway Can Change Memory
titleZh: 为什么走过门口会影响记忆
paras: Have you ever entered a room and forgotten why you went there? This common experience tells us something about memory. One [[basic|basic]] job of the brain is to connect actions with places. Imagine a traveller called Hana at an airport near [[midnight|midnight]]. She sits in a [[public|public]] waiting area and puts her [[boarding-card|boarding card]] beside her cup. She plans to pick it up after putting some [[rubbish|rubbish]] in a bin.

Then Hana sees a sign for the [[restroom|restroom]] and walks through its door. Inside, she forgets about the card. Her brain has not simply stopped working [[properly|properly]]. A new room brings new sights and sounds. The brain may treat this as the start of a new event. Information from the last place can become harder to reach. This sometimes happens when people pass through doorways, although it does not happen every time.

When Hana comes out, she has a [[choice|choice]]: go straight to the drinks [[bar|bar]] or [[return|return]] to her seat. She goes back. Seeing the cup helps her remember the card. The old place offers a useful clue. Our memories are not kept like objects in separate boxes. What we see around us can help us find them again.
zh: 你有没有走进一个房间后，忘了自己为什么要进去？这种常见的经历能让我们了解记忆的一个特点。大脑的一项基本工作，是把行动与地点联系起来。想象一下，一位名叫哈娜的旅客在接近午夜时待在机场。她坐在公共候机区，把登机牌放在杯子旁边。她打算先把一些垃圾扔进垃圾桶，再拿起登机牌。
接着，哈娜看见了洗手间的标志，便走了进去。进门后，她忘记了登机牌的事。这并不意味着她的大脑不再正常工作了。新的房间带来了新的景象和声音。大脑可能把这看作一件新事情的开始。这样一来，与上一个地方有关的信息就可能变得更难想起。人们穿过门口时，有时会出现这种情况，但并不是每次都会发生。
哈娜出来后，可以选择直接去饮品吧台，也可以回到座位。她回去了。看到杯子，让她想起了登机牌。原来的地方提供了一条有用的线索。我们的记忆并不像物品那样，分别存放在一个个盒子里。周围看到的东西，可以帮助我们重新找回记忆。

q.s: Hana plans to put some rubbish in a bin before picking up her boarding card.
q.why: 第一段说她打算扔完垃圾再拿登机牌。

q.s: Walking through a doorway always makes information harder to remember.
q.why: 第二段明确说这种情况并非每次都会发生。

q.s: Hana orders a cold drink after finding her card.
q.why: 文章未提及她找到登机牌后是否点饮料。
